subject: survey design, strip transect, and coverage grid

messages.author: 925ef3a94816cec2
messages.subject: survey design, strip transect, and coverage grid
parts:
Dear distance sampling group,

we are running some designs for a drone survey. The drone has a video camera with field of view 65x40 degrees and we are flying at an altitude of 305m (1000 feet).
Therefore the width should be of 194m (obtained as =305*TAN(RADIANS(65)/2)).

My question is:  as the width is fix, when generating the coverage grid, should we set the distance between grid points equal to the width, so 194m?

I look forward to hearing from you.

Many thanks.

My very best,
Marina

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] survey design, strip transect, and coverage grid
parts:
Marina

I presume you are asking about how to parameterize the coverage grid associated with the design engine (if you are using DistWin) or the dssd​ R package.

You need not specify the spacing of coverage grid points to conform to characteristics of your survey platform.  You should set the spacing of the coverage grid so as to be "representative" of the study area.  The coverage grid will tell you how evenly survey effort is spread across the study area.  In my experience, set the grid point spacing such that there are 1000-5000 points in your coverage grid.  That should satisfy the desire to be representative.

Recognise the smaller the grid point spacing the larger will be the number of points in the coverage grid.  The larger number of points will increase the computation time when investigating your designs.

That's good insight Marina.  If you are worried about poor or uneven coverage near the edges of the study area, having a higher number of grid points will provide more information regarding the edges than a small number of grid points.
